testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When driving, what speed should you use?

options.text: Always drive at the posted speed limit.
Always drive slightly below the posted speed limit.
Adjust your speed based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adjust your speed based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast causes many fatal crashes. You must change your speed to match road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: When exiting a bus during the vehicle control skills test, you must:

options.text: Keep both hands on the handrail.

questions.explanation: When exiting your bus, face the vehicle and use three points of contact at all times. Always hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly will fail the test.

questions.question: When should you shift to a lower gear before going downhill?

options.text: As you go downhill and pick up speed.
Near the bottom of the hill.

questions.explanation: Shift to a lower gear before going downhill. This helps you control the vehicle and use engine braking. Choose a safe speed based on how steep the hill is, how long it is, your vehicle's weight, road conditions, and weather.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection with two left turn lanes, which lane should you use?

options.text: Large vehicles should not turn at intersections with two left turn lanes.

questions.explanation: Large vehicles need extra space to turn left. Use the right left turn lane to begin your turn.

questions.question: When inspecting an enclosed trailer, what should you check about the front?

options.text: It should be free of cracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should be free of cracks.
questions.explanation: When inspecting an enclosed trailer, check the front for damage such as cracks, bulges, or holes.

questions.question: When backing your vehicle into an alley, what should you do first?

options.text: Pull directly into the alley parking space.
Turn your vehicle right to position it directly in front of the alley.
Pull past the alley and stop perpendicular to the outer boundary.
Pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary.
questions.explanation: Pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary. Then back your vehicle straight into the alley parking space.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Drive faster to finish the trip quickly.

questions.explanation: The only safe thing to do when you feel drowsy is to safely pull over and sleep. Artificial stimulants like coffee can be dangerous because fatigue can return suddenly.

questions.question: What are passive railroad crossings?

options.text: Crossings with no traffic control devices.
Crossings with gates that lower when trains approach.
Crossings that large vehicles cannot use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossings with no traffic control devices.
questions.explanation: Passive railroad crossings have no traffic control devices. The driver decides whether it is safe to cross.

questions.question: An open car window in cold weather may show that the driver is:

options.text: Using the heat in their vehicle.

questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs of impaired driving. Drivers who have drunk alcohol, are sleepy, are using drugs, or are ill are hazards to others. An open window in cold weather can indicate impairment.

questions.question: What does Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) mean?

options.text: The total weight of a vehicle and its load
The total weight of a vehicle's tractor only
The total weight of a loaded trailer only
The weight of a tractor and trailer before adding cargo

questions.correctAnswerText: The total weight of a vehicle and its load
questions.explanation: Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) is the total weight of a vehicle plus everything it carries.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to do which of the following?
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset backing to the right, offset backing to the left, driver side parallel parking, regular parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: What is a Gross Vehicle Weight Rating?

options.text: The maximum weight a vehicle can weigh when fully loaded, as stated by the manufacturer.
The maximum weight a single vehicle can pull.
The minimum weight a single vehicle must carry.
The maximum weight that can be loaded onto a single trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum weight a vehicle can weigh when fully loaded, as stated by the manufacturer.
questions.explanation: Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) is the maximum weight of a vehicle and its load as set by the manufacturer.

questions.question: Which statement about distracted driving is true?

options.text: It only happens from physical distractions, not mental ones.
Pre-programming radio stations helps prevent it.
Avoiding complex conversations while driving helps prevent it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoiding complex conversations while driving helps prevent it.
questions.explanation: To reduce distraction while driving, do not have complex or emotional conversations. Pre-program your radio before driving and avoid eating, drinking, or smoking while driving. Remember that mental distractions are just as dangerous as physical distractions.

questions.question: When using your mirrors, you should frequently check your tires for what reason?

options.text: To see if the tires are rolling properly.
To check if the tread is worn enough.
To compare the tire size to other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Check your tires regularly in your mirrors to spot tire fires. Tire fires can start when tires are under-inflated, when dual tires touch each other, or when tires overheat.

questions.question: While driving any vehicle in Kansas, what is the law about texting?

options.text: You cannot send a text but you can read one.
You can send a text but you cannot read one.
You cannot send or read a text.
You can read a text only from your employer.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot send or read a text.
questions.explanation: In Kansas, it is illegal and dangerous to send or read text messages while driving.

questions.question: What color is the low air pressure warning light?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning light. This light is red and may also have a buzzer.

questions.question: When taking the on-road driving test, you must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Complete the test without an accident.
Show that you can use your cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show that you can use your cell phone while driving.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, you must drive safely and responsibly. You must wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs and laws, and finish the test without any accidents or traffic violations.

questions.question: When driving down a steep hill, what should you do?

options.text: Shift into a lower gear, then use the brakes to add extra stopping power from the engine.
Keep downshifting instead of using the brakes.
Drive on the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift into a lower gear, then use the brakes to add extra stopping power from the engine.
questions.explanation: Use the engine's braking power as your main way to control speed on a downgrade. Shift to a lower gear before going down the hill. Use the brakes only when you need extra slowing or stopping.

questions.question: When are most drivers the least alert?
questions.explanation: Fatigue and tiredness are major problems when driving at night. Most drivers are the least alert at night, especially after midnight.

questions.question: If you use a helper while backing a vehicle, where should they stand?

options.text: In front of the passenger side.
In front of the driver side.
On the side of the truck.
Near the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the back of the truck.
questions.explanation: If you use a helper while backing, they should stand near the back of the vehicle where you can see them. Before backing, agree on hand signals with your helper. Have a signal that means "stop."

questions.question: Where can you find the tire load rating?

options.text: On the inside of the driver's door
On the side of each tire

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side of each tire
questions.explanation: The tire load rating is the maximum weight a tire can safely carry at a given pressure. You can find this number printed on the side of each tire.

questions.question: To leave a stop as safely as possible, you should park:

options.text: So that you must back up to leave your parking space.
So that you can pull forward to leave your parking space.
On the side of a roadway, not in a parking lot.
By backing into a parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: So that you can pull forward to leave your parking space.
questions.explanation: Backing up is dangerous. Whenever possible, park so you can pull forward when leaving. This reduces the risk of hitting something behind your vehicle.

questions.question: How does doubling your speed from 20 mph to 40 mph affect your braking distance?
questions.explanation: When you double your speed from 20 to 40 mph, your braking distance increases four times. Higher speeds mean more power in a crash and much longer distances to stop.

questions.question: Shaded areas of the road:

options.text: Usually do not contain moisture, so they can't freeze.
Will remain slick after ice on other areas of the road has melted.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will remain slick after ice on other areas of the road has melted.
questions.explanation: Shaded areas get less sunlight and stay cooler longer. Ice in these areas melts slower than ice in sunny areas. So shaded spots can still be icy and slippery after ice has melted elsewhere.

questions.question: If confronted by an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.

questions.explanation: If you meet an aggressive driver, get out of their way. Do not make eye contact or gesture at them. Once you are safe, report the driver to the police or proper authorities.

questions.question: A vehicle should be equipped with all of the following, except:

options.text: Warning devices for parked vehicles, such as flares.

questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must carry emergency equipment. This includes at least one fire extinguisher, spare electrical fuses (unless the vehicle has circuit breakers), and warning devices like triangles or flares. A spotlight is not required.

questions.question: Carriers must keep fuel records for IFTA quarterly fuel tax returns for:
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicle operators must register under the International Registration Plan (IRP) and International Fuel Tax Agreement (IFTA). These programs track registration fees and fuel taxes based on where you drive. You must keep mileage and fuel records for four years.

questions.question: If hydraulic brakes fail, you can reduce speed by:

options.text: Letting the truck run out of gas.

questions.explanation: If your hydraulic brakes fail, shift into a lower gear. This uses the engine to slow your vehicle down.

questions.question: Once stopped during the stop/start maneuver, you should:

options.text: Keep the vehicle in first gear.

questions.explanation: During the stop/start maneuver on the driving test, apply the parking brake once stopped. Shift into neutral or park. Park parallel to the curb and do not block any driveways or intersections.

questions.question: When exiting your vehicle, you:

options.text: Must maintain four points of contact with the vehicle.
May turn to face the road before your exit is complete.
Must be facing away from the vehicle.

questions.explanation: When exiting during the basic vehicle control skills test, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. On a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may cause you to fail the test.

questions.question: When should you use the parking brake?

options.text: Every time you park your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you park your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Use the parking brake every time you park your vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do in an emergency stop?

options.text: Lock the wheels and skid to a stop.
Brake so your vehicle stays in a straight line.
Expect your vehicle to slow down faster than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake so your vehicle stays in a straight line.
questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, brake in a way that keeps your vehicle going straight. This lets you maintain control and turn if needed.

questions.question: How do you apply the parking brake in a newer vehicle?

options.text: Pull out a diamond-shaped yellow knob.
Pull out a round red knob.
Pull out a square green knob.
Pull out a black round knob.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull out a diamond-shaped yellow knob.
questions.explanation: In newer vehicles, the parking brake is a diamond-shaped yellow knob. Pull it out to apply the brakes and push it in to release them.

questions.question: What can federal inspectors do if they find your vehicle unsafe?

options.text: Take you to a garage to have it fixed.
Request that you fix the problems.
Stop the vehicle from being driven until it is fixed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the vehicle from being driven until it is fixed.
questions.explanation: If a federal or state inspector finds a vehicle unsafe, they can take it out of service until the problems are fixed.

questions.question: What does a one-way check valve do?

options.text: Drains water and oil from the air tanks.
Stops air from leaking out if the compressor breaks.
Turns on emergency brakes when there is a leak.
Holds the spring brakes in place until you use them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops air from leaking out if the compressor breaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve is placed between the air compressor and the main tank. It stops air from escaping if the compressor leaks.

questions.question: What does the emergency brake system use?

options.text: Parts from both parking and service brake systems.
Parts unique only to the emergency brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts from both parking and service brake systems.
questions.explanation: An air brake system has three parts: service brakes, parking brakes, and emergency brakes. The emergency brake system uses parts from both the parking and service brake systems.

questions.question: What do anti-lock brakes do?

options.text: Prevent the wheels from locking up.
Stop a vehicle from speeding uphill.
Stop a vehicle from speeding downhill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent the wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: Anti-lock brakes prevent your wheels from locking when you brake hard.

questions.question: How do you do an offset back/right parking maneuver?

options.text: Go straight forward, then back up to the right.
Go straight forward, then back up to the left.
Go forward to the right, then back in a straight line.
Go forward to the left, then back in a straight line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go straight forward, then back up to the right.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/right parking maneuver, go straight forward first, then back up to the right. Your vehicle must fit completely inside the parking space.

questions.question: Which action does NOT cause a distraction while driving?
questions.explanation: Anything that takes your attention away from the road is a distraction. This includes eating, drinking, smoking, and adjusting the radio or climate controls. Checking your mirrors is a safe driving habit.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel tired and are yawning frequently?

options.text: Pull over and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and take a nap.
questions.explanation: Frequent yawning means you are tired. The only safe thing to do is stop and sleep. Coffee and other stimulants will wear off and make you even more tired later.

questions.question: Poisonous fumes can enter the cab because of:

options.text: Using the wrong type of fuel.
Not enough oil in the engine.
Tires that are not filled enough.

questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is very dangerous. It can allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should NOT:
questions.explanation: If you must drive through fog, slow down. Use your low beam headlights and fog lights. Turn on your four-way flashers.

questions.question: A driver should always:

options.text: Drive faster than the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Watch the road ahead for dangers. Plan what you will do if a danger becomes a problem.

questions.question: Air entering air storage tanks may contain:
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks in the brake system usually have water and compressor oil in them. These materials can damage the braking system if they build up. Tanks have drains to remove them.

questions.question: When driving through a work zone, you should:
questions.explanation: Follow the posted speed limits in work zones. Slow down if road or weather conditions are bad. Slow down even more if workers are near the road.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in:
questions.explanation: Check the air pressure in both brake systems before your trip. It should build from 85 to 100 psi in both systems in about 45 seconds.

questions.question: During a walk-around inspection, brake drums should have no cracks larger than ____ of the friction area width.
questions.explanation: Check the brake drums before your trip. Do not drive if any brake drum has a crack larger than one half the width of the friction area.

questions.question: During the basic vehicle control skills test:

options.text: Points are taken away for each pull-up.
You can do three pull-ups per maneuver.
You get points for a pull-up only if you exit the vehicle first.
Too many pull-ups will be counted as errors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Too many pull-ups will be counted as errors.
questions.explanation: During the test, one pull-up is allowed without penalty. However, too many pull-ups will count as errors.

questions.question: The main reason to inspect your vehicle before a trip is:
questions.explanation: The main reason to inspect your vehicle is to keep yourself and others safe on the road. Safety inspections before every trip are required by law.

questions.question: About winter driving, which of the following is NOT true:

options.text: Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread.
Rear tires need at least 2/32 inch of tread.
Use a gauge to check tread depth on each tire.

questions.explanation: In winter, your tires need good tread. Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread in every major groove. Rear tires need at least 2/32 inch. Use a gauge to check the tread depth.
